title: Equivalence: G-equivariant (co)sheaves and functors on ]X/G[
body_html:
Equivalence: $G$-equivariant (co)sheaves as functors on $]X/G[$

Lemma. The category of $G$-equivariant $\mathscr{C}$-valued sheaves on $X$ is equivalent to $\underline{\mathrm{Fun}}(]X/G[,\mathscr{C})$. Dually, the category of $G$-equivariant $\mathscr{C}$-valued cosheaves on $X$ is equivalent to $\underline{\mathrm{Fun}}([X/G],\mathscr{C})$.

In particular, taking $G = \{e\}$ recovers the equivalences $\Sh(X,\mathscr{C}) = \underline{\mathrm{Fun}}(]X[,\mathscr{C})$ and $\Cosh(X,\mathscr{C}) = \underline{\mathrm{Fun}}([X],\mathscr{C})$.

Sketch of the equivalence (sheaf case)

Given $(V,a) \in \Sh_G(X,\mathscr{C})$, define $F : \,]X/G[\, \to \mathscr{C}$ by $F(E) := V_E$ and, for $g \in \Hom_{]X/G[}(E,E')$ (i.e.\ $gE \preceq E'$), $$F(g) := r^V_{gE,E'} \circ a^V_{g,E}.$$

Functoriality (i.e.\ $F(h) \circ F(g) = F(hg)$) follows by chasing the equivariance axiom of $a^V$ and the transitivity of $r^V$. Conversely, given $F : \,]X/G[\, \to \mathscr{C}$, set $V_E := F(E)$, $r^V_{E,E'} := F(e : E \to E')$, and $a^V_{g,E} := F(g : E \to gE)$; this gives a $G$-equivariant sheaf. The two constructions are mutually inverse.

The cosheaf case is dual.
